sources.title: Berkowitz, Bour, Davy & Odling (2000) Scaling of fracture connectivity in geological formations. GRL 27(14), 2061-2064
sources.used_for: Connectivity framework for the topology candidate class (exponent a, fractal dimension D, density, critical length)
sources.status: abstract verified on publisher page; full text read via a ResearchGate copy
sources.evidence: Abstract: connectivity depends on scale of measurement for a < D+1, independent of scale for a > D+1; "Analysis of the San Andreas fault system shows that a < D+1 and that the connectivity threshold is reached only at a critical length scale." Text: a = 2.1, D = 1.65, beta = 0.0085; "connectivity is expected for L > 21 km"; "the above results are statistical, and provide connectivity estimates on averages, rather than on particular realizations".

sources.title: Faulds & Hinz (2015) Favorable tectonic and structural settings of geothermal systems in the Great Basin Region, Western USA. Proc. World Geothermal Congress
sources.used_for: Structural-setting statistics for step-overs, terminations, intersections; regional kinematic context
sources.evidence: Of ~250 categorised fields: step-overs/relay ramps ~32 %, normal-fault terminations 25 %, intersections 22 %, accommodation zones 9 %, transfer zones 5 %, pull-aparts 3 %, bends 2 %, major range-front faults 1 %; ~39 % of 426 systems are blind.

sources.evidence: "In Wesnousky (2006, 2008), the largest strike-slip step broken in rupture was 4 km." Concerns strike-slip earthquake ruptures, not mapped-fault connectivity.

sources.title: Hermant, Kiersnowski & Bellanger (2025) Using Deep Learning to Map Quaternary Faults in Western USA. Proc. 50th Workshop on Geothermal Reservoir Engineering, Stanford University (SGP-TR-229)
sources.used_for: Competition benchmark background, 150-400 m USGS-vs-LiDAR scarp offset motivating H27-4 tip-shadow pruning, and false-positive geomorphology taxonomy
sources.evidence: Compares FaultSEG (PR-AUC 0.595) vs siUNET (0.449, 487,297 params) on 1/3 arc-sec 3DEP LiDAR DEM, slope, and Sentinel-2 B8A. Documents 150-400 m positional offsets between USGS QFaults and LiDAR scarps (Fig. 2 & Fig. 9B), non-LiDAR DEM slope artifacts, and false positives on paleo-shorelines/beach ridges (Silver et al., 2011), canyon rims, and stream boundaries.

sources.status: page verified; direct zip VERIFIED OBTAINABLE from a GitHub runner on 2026-10-02 (HTTP 206, application/zip, zip magic PK, 32,371,696 bytes, Last-Modified 2026-02-23); not downloaded into this repo
sources.evidence: Scope statement: faults with "geological evidence of coseismic surface deformation in large earthquakes during the past 1.6 million years" (Quaternary only), which is why a Quaternary-fault catalogue cannot contain older/unlisted bedrock faults. Direct link: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/static/lfs/nshm/qfaults/Qfaults_GIS.zip Discrepancy: the page text says '16 MB ZIP' but the server reports 32,371,696 bytes (docs/data/feed.json).

sources.title: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP), 1-meter DEM downloadable data collection
sources.used_for: Official provenance/context for the owner-mirrored LiDAR-derived terrain descriptors and H28-2 multi-scale scarp hypothesis
sources.status: official catalog page read 2026-10-02; public-domain description and 1-m bare-earth DEM coverage verified; tile binary not retrieved from this sandbox
sources.evidence: USGS record states 1-m 3DEP DEMs are a tiled bare-earth elevation collection produced from high-resolution lidar and identifies 3DEP products as public domain. Repository lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif is a hash-pinned owner mirror/derivative, not a direct USGS download in this session. The local DEM inventory has 716 confirmed links, 706 successful derived tiles, 10 failed tiles (see data_cache/dem_links.json and pinned sibling metadata).
